label: r4c1
name: r2c1 with gamma 0.9
hypothesis: Only change from r2c1: gamma goes from 0.95 to 0.9. Gamma 0.99 made seeds collapse to DONE because random early placements add up to a large negative return. A shorter horizon makes stopping early look less attractive, while each correct cell still pays straight away. The exact-build bonus is paid at the DONE step itself, so it is not discounted. Expect a mean above 0.79 with no collapsed seed. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.79.
last_analysis: The observed target is shifted by X/2 in x. Adding a rolled copy of the input (dual-frame) fixes this: dev success went from 0 to 0.59. The learned circular row conv also worked but scored lower (0.35). Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 at 256 envs gave the best result so far (r2c1, 0.79, both seeds close). Most failures look like seeds collapsing to DONE-only. That happened with 1 epoch (0.21/0.00), with gamma 0.99 (0.00/0.32 and 0.00/0.00), and in one seed with 128 envs. The sign is consistent: a longer horizon makes it look worse to keep placing randomly than to stop, and more frequent noisy updates lock in that choice. The two architecture additions (dilated conv, global broadcast) scored lower, partly through fewer samples and partly through seed luck. For the last round, I keep the r2c1 network and recipe and change one thing per trial to make collapse less likely: shorter horizon, more entropy, or near-uniform output initialisation.
